title.narrative: Strengthening Inclusive Adaptation Capacity in Solomon Islands (SIAC-SI)

description.narrative: Active

The Strengthening Inclusive Adaptation Capacity in Solomon Islands (SIAC-SI) project is a nationally aligned, regionally supported initiative designed to enhance the Solomon Islands’ capacity to plan, implement, and finance inclusive and climate-resilient development. The project is implemented by the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), in close collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change, Disaster Management and Meteorology (MECDM). GGGI is the executing entity and signatory to the donor funding agreement with the Government of Australia through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), which serves as the sole financing partner for the project. SIAC-SI is structured as a two-phase program to enable a phased, systematic, and country-driven approach to developing the country’s first National Adaptation Plan (NAP). The project responds to institutional, technical, and financing gaps in the climate adaptation landscape of the Solomon Islands, while supporting national obligations under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement. Phase 1 includes establishing project governance arrangements, supporting early institutional preparedness within MECDM, and initiating procurement planning for key activities under Phase 2. The second phase focuses on full implementation of the NAP development process. It includes the design and rollout of national-level Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessments (CRVAs) for selected priority sectors, and the implementation of Solomon Islands Integrated Vulnerability Assessments (SIIVA) at the community level in selected provinces. Other components include institutional strengthening for coordination and planning, capacity development, integration of GEDSI principles into adaptation processes, and the development of a NAP investment roadmap. The phase will culminate in the formal submission of the Solomon Islands’ first NAP to the UNFCCC.

The objective of the SIAC-SI project is to strengthen the Solomon Islands’ institutional, technical, and financial capacity to plan, implement, and finance inclusive, evidence-based, and climate-resilient development through the preparation and implementation of the country’s first National Adaptation Plan (NAP). The project aims to operationalize a structured and phased approach to national adaptation planning by supporting the development of foundational assessments, institutional frameworks, and financing strategies that align with national priorities, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Through its two-phase structure, SIAC-SI seeks to build systems and capacities that enable the Government of Solomon Islands to integrate climate risk into national planning processes, address the needs of the most vulnerable, and mobilize resources for long-term adaptation action.
